newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, S.Korea wary of Taiwan pact with N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: Japan, S.Korea wary of Taiwan pact with N.Korea.

text.p: The leaders of Japan and South Korea voiced concern on Saturday over planned shipments of nuclear waste from Taiwan to North Korea.

Visiting South Korean President Kim Young-sam told Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto in this southern Japanese resort that he was concerned about the environmental impact of the planned shipments of low-level nuclear waste.
"It requires sophisticated technology to process nuclear waste," a Japanese foriegn ministry official quoted Kim as telling Hashimoto during a lunch meeting.
"I am concered about a grave impact on the environment of the shipments of low-level nuclear waste from Taiwan to North Korea," Kim said.
Hashimoto said he shared the same concerns.
Earlier this month, the state-run Taiwan Power Co said it would ship 60,000 barrels of Taiwan's nuclear waste to North Korea and was seeking similiar deals with Russia and the Marshall Islands.
Under the deal, Taiwan would ship the nuclear waste to North Korea within two years.
The contract says Taiwan Power has an option to ship a total of up to 200,000 barrels of nuclear waste to North Korea.

Pyongyang entered a landmark pact with Washington in 1995, agreeing to allow international inspections and replace its Soviet-era reactors with modern Seoul-financed light-water ones that produce less weapons-grade plutonium.
